restatement: The SLA report incorrectly flags cancelled jobs as breached because the service treats them as still in-flight, causing their end time to be measured against `now` indefinitely.
risks: False-positive SLA breaches clutter operational dashboards and mask real failures
SLA margin calculations remain negative for cancelled jobs until they are manually cleaned up

sites.why: `finished_at` decides when an SLA timer stops. It explicitly checks for `st.DONE` and `st.FAILED` but omits `CANCELLED`. Since `CANCELLED` is a terminal status in `jobs/status.py`, it should be grouped with the others so the function returns `job.ended_at` instead of falling through to `return now`.
